```{python}
#| label: cargar-suplemento
from pathlib import Path
import sys

ROOT = Path.cwd().parent if Path.cwd().name == "docs" else Path.cwd()
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "docs" / "lancet"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import render_helpers as rh
from report_helpers import kpis

counts = rh.summary_counts("supplement", "en")
kpis([
    (str(counts["equations"]), "Numbered equations of the extended methods (STIX images from equations_lancet.py)"),
    (str(counts["tables"]), "Supplementary table parts (S1 to S9)"),
    (str(counts["figures"]), "Supplementary figures; S2–S5 and S7–S9 generated by docs/lancet/figuras_suplementarias.py"),
    (str(counts["references"]), "Supplementary references"),
])
```

The supplement opens with the extended methods (sections A1 to A11) and continues with the complementary results, the tables and the figures, in the same order as the submitted document (`supplement_en.docx`). The text and tables come from `docs/lancet/data/contenido_v10.json`; the equations are the images composed with the STIX family that the document prints, at a single type size. Figures S1 (data flow) and S6 (territorial maps) are plates inherited from revision 09; the rest are regenerated from `docs/lancet/data/`. In figure S7 and in figure 4d of the article, the commune comparison uses `communes_public.csv`, an extract without identifiers in which cells with 1 to 4 records are masked variable by variable, so that the points shown coincide with those of the manuscript; the sensitivity to the count threshold (S7d) is read precomputed on the complete commune file, which is not published.
